source.title: Per-example gradients: a new frontier for understanding and improving optimizers

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests optimizer variants and per-example gradient methods, but it does not test whether networks that fit arbitrary labels generalize on natural labels or any of the eight claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer training and evaluation losses, batch-size scaling, and gradient-statistic measurements. These do not measure the claim’s named natural-label generalization gap, comparisons, or memorized-example effects; the optimizer findings are outside the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The batch-size sweeps measure held-out language-model loss at matched sample budgets, bearing on V5 in a C4 transformer setting. Appendix E.2.3–E.2.4 sets steps inversely proportional to batch size, keeping total token exposure approximately fixed. The record incorrectly excludes these results. Comparisons among Adam and sign variants do not test V4's adaptive-versus-SGD comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors conclude that per-example gradient statistics are tractable, that delaying sign improves the tested sign optimizers, and that mean-squared-gradient information serves Adam preconditioning better than variance information on their workload. These conclusions concern optimization and evaluation-loss trajectories, without establishing a separate generalization-gap mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: Studies per-example gradient transformations and optimizer behavior, not the claim’s natural-label generalization or memorization comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports differences across optimizer variants, batch sizes, and learning-rate scaling rules, but these are outside the mapped claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: SignEMA achieves the best evaluation-loss trajectory among the three sign placements, followed by SignSGD and MicroSignSGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Delaying the sign operation improves performance and stability among these sign-based optimizers on the tested transformer workload.

fits_no_version.finding: At B = 64, Adam reaches evaluation loss 3.06, unmodified MicroAdam 3.16, and filtered, clipped MicroAdamMSQ 3.05. Clipped MicroAdam and MicroAdamVar reach 3.10 and 3.20.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mean-squared-gradient preconditioning performs better than variance-dominated alternatives on this workload, with filtering and clipping needed for MicroAdamMSQ stability.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-example gradient computations have modest overhead on transformer workloads, and computational graph surgery can reduce implementation costs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture and implementation determine the computational feasibility of per-example gradient statistics.

record.problems: The reported optimizer comparisons use a single 151M-parameter decoder-only transformer language model on C4; the authors identify broader architecture and batch-size study as needed for some gradient-statistic findings. The paper does not report uncertainty estimates for these results in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No results were eligible for rows under the defined claim versions. The optimizer performance and gradient-statistic findings are described under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out performance.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus standard SGD or momentum SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Image classifiers, longer training as a remedy, and normalization changes. The study uses matched token exposure rather than reporting complete dataset epochs.

missing.what: Add V5 rows for Adam evaluation-loss curves across B = 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 under square-root learning-rate scaling, distinguishing intermediate-batch agreement, small-batch crossover, and large-batch breakdown or divergence. The record's blanket exclusion of batch scaling is incorrect.
missing.locator: Figure 6 top left; Appendix D.1 and Figure 10; budget and schedule details in Appendix E.2.3–E.2.4.

missing.what: Add V5 rows for batch-size sweeps of MicroAdam, MicroAdamMSQ, and MicroAdamVar, including the clipped variants. Record evaluation loss at common sample exposure, learning-rate scaling, clipping, and stability; do not substitute scaling-rule success alone for held-out performance.
missing.locator: Section 3.2.1–3.2.3 and Figure 6; Appendix D.2 and Figure 11.

record.verdict_notes: No extracted rows exist to fix. Batch-size findings belong under V5 rather than entirely under fits_no_version. Equal token exposure permits comparison at matched data budgets, but scaled learning rates, warmup, and weight decay make these tests of adapted recipes. Exact losses for individual batch sizes should be recovered from the figures; they are not supplied numerically in the text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance under the specified tuning conditions.
Large-batch versus small-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the train-test gap.
Effects of removing memorized training examples on test accuracy.

relationships.condition: Large batches beyond the universal scaling regime, with learning rates scaled from B = 64 and approximately fixed token exposure.
relationships.reason: Based on the text, since rows are missing: Section 3.2.1 reports breakdown at larger batches across the Adam family; Appendix D.1 explicitly reports increasingly different curves and eventual divergence for Adam.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports increasingly different learning curves and eventual Adam divergence beyond the scaling regime, but the comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: Small-to-intermediate batches with optimizer-specific learning-rate scaling.
relationships.reason: Based on the text, since rows are missing: MicroAdam has similar evaluation-loss curves for B = 8–64 with linear scaling; Adam has similar intermediate-to-late curves for B = 16–128 with square-root scaling. Smaller learning rates improve agreement.
relationships.display_finding: Similar evaluation-loss curves were reported with linear scaling for MicroAdam and square-root scaling for Adam, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
